claims.claim: `astar_fixed` fails the first time an action misbehaves (slip or skid)
claims.measured: success 4.6% [3.8%, 5.5%] (110/2400) at p = 0 vs 0.6% (61/9600 runs on 2400 maps) at p ≥ 0.1; map-paired sign test p = 3.1e-33 (109 maps worse, 0 better at p ≥ 0.1); 6141/6141 runs with a slip or skid failed
claims.details:
Experiment `slip_sweep`; sizes pooled: 10×10, 15×15, 20×20; scenarios: random_rubble, collapsed_building, flooded_zone, maze_corridors; slip p ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4}.

Rule: ✅ if the success rate at p ≥ 0.1 is below the one at p = 0, the drop is significant in an exact two-sided sign test over maps (α = 0.05; per map: success at p = 0 minus mean success at p ≥ 0.1; with one p this is the exact McNemar test) **and** every run with at least one slip or skid failed; ⚠️ if the drop is not significant or some runs survived a slip or skid; ❌ if the success rate does not drop. The map is the unit because every p reuses the same maps (common random numbers); the per-p Wilson intervals below are each over distinct maps.

Runs with ≥ 1 non-arrived outcome: 6141; survived: 0 (a run can survive only if the deviation itself lands on the survivor).

Abort reasons: *after a slip/skid* = `aborted` with slips + skids > 0 (deviation from the path); *debris ahead* = `aborted` with none (the next path cell turned out to be debris; no replanning).

| slip p | success (Wilson 95 % CI) | aborted after slip/skid | aborted at debris ahead | budget | unreachable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4.6% [3.8%, 5.5%] (110/2400) | 342 | 1948 | 0 | 0 |
| 0.1 | 1.8% [1.3%, 2.4%] (42/2400) | 988 | 1370 | 0 | 0 |
| 0.2 | 0.5% [0.3%, 0.9%] (12/2400) | 1374 | 1014 | 0 | 0 |
| 0.3 | 0.2% [0.1%, 0.5%] (6/2400) | 1628 | 766 | 0 | 0 |
| 0.4 | 0.0% [0.0%, 0.2%] (1/2400) | 1809 | 590 | 0 | 0 |

Caveats: (1) p = 0 is not free of misbehaviour: high-slip terrain ('~' cells) keeps its own slip parameter (0.4) at every p, so 342/2400 runs at p = 0 had a slip or skid. (2) `astar_fixed` also aborts when it senses debris on its next path cell, so its success at p = 0 is already only 4.6% [3.8%, 5.5%] (110/2400) (1948 aborts at debris ahead): most of its failures come from debris it did not know about, not from a misbehaving action. The verdict covers the slip/skid part of the claim only.

claims.claim: `andor`'s wasted-move advantage over `astar_replan` survives matched tie-breaking
claims.measured: matched diagonal +0.11 [-0.12, +0.35] ⚠️ (CI ±0.24), matched plain +0.56 [+0.20, +0.91] ❌ (CI ±0.36) moves over p > 0 (2400 maps; equivalence margin ±0.5); single-factor effects: andor diagonal − fixed -3.64 [-4.40, -2.89] ✅, A* diagonal − g -3.20 [-3.91, -2.49] ✅; unmatched (H3) -3.09 [-3.81, -2.37] ✅; identical steps + cells explored at p > 0: (a) 92.1% (8839/9600), (b) 87.9% (8442/9600), (H3) 25.6% (2454/9600) (tie-break matching is approximate); refuted: a matched CI lies above 0
claims.details:
Experiments `slip_sweep` (default planner: AND-OR D13 diagonal tie-break, A* larger-g then FIFO) and `tiebreak_ablation` (the same missions with the tie-breaks swapped), restricted to r = 1, eager replanning, no aftershocks. Task seeds do not depend on the planner overrides, so every ablation run pairs 1:1 with the slip-sweep run of the same map, outcome stream and slip p (pairing across blocks on scenario, rows, cols, slip_p, sensor_radius, replan_mode, aftershock_q, replicate, seed).

Why: at p = 0 nothing slips except on high-slip '~' terrain, which keeps its own slip parameter (0.4) at every block p (only in flooded_zone here: 1949/2400 of the runs there at p = 0 had a slip or skid); everywhere else AND-OR has no contingency to plan for and reduces to a greedy shortest-route search on the optimistic belief, so a difference there (H3's p = 0 row; the (H3) column of the p = 0 row below) is path choice, not contingency planning. Under the optimistic-unknown assumption many routes are equally short, and which one an agent takes (its tie-break) decides how often it walks into unseen debris. (a) and (b) compare the agents with matched tie-breaks (only approximately matched: see the manipulation check below); (c) and (d) measure each tie-break's own effect. On common pairs H3 = (a) + (d) = (b) + (c) (approximately here, since each difference uses the runs where both of its sides succeeded).

| comparison | a | b |
|---|---|---|
| (a) matched, diagonal | `andor` tie_break=diagonal (`slip_sweep`) | `astar_replan` astar_tie_break=diagonal (`tiebreak_ablation`) |
| (b) matched, plain | `andor` tie_break=fixed (`tiebreak_ablation`) | `astar_replan` astar_tie_break=g (`slip_sweep`) |
| (c) andor diagonal − fixed | `andor` tie_break=diagonal (`slip_sweep`) | `andor` tie_break=fixed (`tiebreak_ablation`) |
| (d) A* diagonal − g | `astar_replan` astar_tie_break=diagonal (`tiebreak_ablation`) | `astar_replan` astar_tie_break=g (`slip_sweep`) |
| (H3) unmatched | `andor` tie_break=diagonal (`slip_sweep`) | `astar_replan` astar_tie_break=g (`slip_sweep`) |

Difference = a − b in wasted moves (successful runs on both sides), map as the unit (per-map mean over the p > 0 values, as in H3); Student-t 95 % CI, paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test over maps. Rule: ✅ if the CIs of both matched comparisons (a) and (b) lie below 0 over p > 0; ❌ if either lies above 0, or if both lie entirely inside ±0.5 moves (equivalence margin chosen before the final full run, not pre-registered — docs/plan.md D21; TOST-style: no practically relevant advantage once tie-breaking is matched); ⚠️ otherwise (a CI contains 0 but is too wide to show equivalence: underpowered, not refuted). p = 0 is shown separately and is not part of the verdict. meta.Methods: success rates with Wilson 95 % intervals; means with Student-t 95 % intervals; paired comparisons on identical maps and outcome / noise streams (a task seed depends only on base seed, scenario, size and replicate) with a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test; pooled paired comparisons use the map as the unit (per-map mean difference; n = maps, not pairs). The noise draws are paired per (step, cell): one uniform per grid cell per step, the same in every mission on that map.
meta.Verdicts: ✅ supported, ❌ refuted, ⚠️ inconclusive or not measured. Thresholds are constants in `rescue/config.py` fixed before the full run; no experiment was tuned toward a verdict.

claims.claim: the greedy nearest-first order is within 10.0% of the optimal tour
claims.details:
Block `multi`: k survivors at known locations (the core map plus k − 1 extra survivors). Greedy tour = true-map BFS length of the nearest-first visiting order from the start; optimal tour = the shortest over all k! orders; both on the initial true map (the oracle the agent's greedy order approximates on its belief). One value per map; Student-t 95 % CI of the mean ratio. For k ≤ 2 greedy is optimal by construction (both orders share the survivor-to-survivor leg), so only k ≥ 3 can test the claim.

claims.measured: ε_fp = 0.05: 100.0% [99.5%, 100.0%] (800/800) ✅; ε_fp = 0.1: 100.0% [99.5%, 100.0%] (800/800) ✅; at ε_fp = 0.1 (informational): steps cost +46.53 steps [+40.79, +52.27] over 800 maps (800 pairs), paired t p = 1.1e-49, Wilcoxon p = 1.4e-72, fallback in 266/800 missions, Σ bumps 1688
claims.details:
Block `noisy_fp` (round 2): the debris sensor reports a true DEBRIS cell as OPEN with probability ε (here ε = 0.1) and a true OPEN cell as DEBRIS with probability ε_fp (two-sided noise; survivor cells, the robot's own cell and a cell a bump touched are never misreported); the belief is the two-sided Bayes map (`ProbBelief`). A false positive can raise a free cell over the debris threshold (a phantom wall); when no target is reachable under the threshold, `SearchAgent` falls back to relaxed passability (only near-certain debris blocks) before giving up. A fallback is counted once per episode (a switch from strict to relaxed passability; a target re-selection made while relaxed that falls back again is not counted). `search_andor` re-selects more often while relaxed (a cell of its plan envelope, which holds skid cells off the main path, turning near-certain debris triggers it), so the fallback counts of the two agents measure partly different things and are not directly comparable. ε_fp = 0 replays block `noisy` at the same ε (same maps and streams).

Rule: at every false-positive rate 0 < ε_fp ≤ 0.1 of the block, ✅ if `search_andor`'s success rate is ≥ 95.0%; ⚠️ if it is below but the Wilson 95 % upper bound reaches 95.0%; ❌ if the upper bound is below it. Overall ✅ only if every level is ✅, ❌ if any level is ❌, else ⚠️ (also ⚠️ "not measured" without runs at ε_fp = 0.1). The steps cost (paired ε_fp − 0 on the same map, both missions successful, map as the unit), the fallback usage and the bumps are reported without a verdict: no threshold was fixed for them before the run.

figures.title: Multi mode: one survivor rescued, the robot heading to the second of three
figures.caption: `multi` with k = 3, step 20 (step budget 1,728). The survivor at (3,9) has just been rescued (green ring and tick). The robot now heads to the nearest remaining known survivor at (4,4), flagged. The third survivor is at the top left.

figures.title: Noisy mode: three bumps into unseen debris, and seen-open cells shaded by their debris probability
figures.caption: `noisy` with ε = 0.1, step 18, just after the third bump (red crosses). Each bump revealed debris the sensor had missed. The hatched cells were read OPEN, and the denser the hatch, the higher their remaining debris probability (legend under the metrics, 0.001 to 0.5).
